pageCache.text:
Co-Headteachers’ Welcome
Cirencester Deer Park School is a special place to learn, grow and succeed. Visitors often remark on the distinctive atmosphere of the school: a sense of energy, ambition and belonging that is felt throughout our community. We are proud of this. At Deer Park, our shared vision is to be the best we can be every day, guided by our core values of trust, kindness and determination.
Our curriculum is designed to inspire, challenge and support every pupil. Through a broad, balanced and ambitious education, we equip young people with the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to thrive both in school and beyond. We want every pupil to believe in their potential and achieve more than they may have thought possible.
At the heart of this experience are our talented and dedicated staff. As passionate subject specialists, our teachers create learning opportunities that are engaging, purposeful and intellectually challenging. They encourage curiosity, resilience and independence, helping pupils develop habits that will serve them well throughout their lives.
From the moment pupils join Deer Park, they become part of a supportive and caring community. Our experienced Pastoral Team, including a dedicated Year Leader for each year group, works closely with teaching staff, our Inclusion Team and our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Team to ensure every pupil feels safe, valued and supported. We are committed to helping every young person flourish academically, socially and emotionally.
Learning at Deer Park extends far beyond the classroom. Our extensive extra-curricular programme offers something for everyone, with opportunities to develop new skills, pursue interests and create lasting memories. Whether it is performing in a school musical, competing in sports teams, participating in Duke of Edinburgh, joining clubs such as Science Club or Tech Team, taking on leadership roles, or exploring the world through educational visits, pupils are encouraged to make the most of every opportunity available to them.
We have high expectations for all our pupils, regardless of their starting point, and are committed to helping everyone realise their potential. Deer Park is a school where remarkable young people are supported to achieve remarkable things, and where strong relationships and a shared commitment to excellence underpins all that we do.
Having been members of the school’s leadership team since 2012, it is a privilege to serve as Acting Co-Headteachers of Cirencester Deer Park School especially as the school celebrates its 60th anniversary as a comprehensive school in 2026. We are immensely proud of our pupils, staff and wider community, and of everything we achieve together. We hope this website gives you a sense of our values, ambitions and aspirations, and we warmly invite you to visit us and experience Deer Park for yourself.
Whether you are a prospective pupil and family, a prospective colleague, or someone interested in our wider community, we look forward to welcoming you.
Helen Howe (nee Charlesworth) and Liz Lang Co-Headteachers

pageCache.pageTitle: How We Talk - Cirencester Deer Park School
pageCache.text:
How We Talk
An organisation is ultimately defined by its culture rather than its strategy. No matter how innovative or well-planned a strategy may be, it will not succeed without the right culture to support it. When a positive culture is deeply embedded, it becomes second nature—shaping behaviours, routines, and interactions in an organic way.
Building and maintaining a strong culture is challenging but essential. To do so, it must be broken down into clear expectations and behaviours that are intentionally modelled and reinforced.
At Deer Park, we are committed to fostering a culture where every member of our school community feels safe, happy, and able to succeed. While many aspects of our culture are well established, we recognize the need for continuous reinforcement. Our expectations around behaviour play a key role in this, ensuring that all pupils, whether new or returning, understand what it means to be part of a positive and supportive environment.
The ‘How We Talk’ poster below reflects our pupils’ voices, along with the collaborative efforts of our staff, to define the ways we should – and should not – communicate with one another.
We believe this guidance is essential in upholding the values of our school community, and we encourage everyone to embrace it as part of our commitment to being the best we can be every day.

Our Mission
Deer Park’s mission, the reason why we exist is to enable everyone to be the best they can be every day. This mission is not restricted to a time or a place, nor indeed a particular group of people. It is a daily goal for everyone, “to be the best we can be every day”.
Our Aims
Ask any family what they want for their children from their education and schooling and it is likely to distil down into three key aims, “I want my child to be safe, be happy and be successful”. These are our school aims for every one of our pupils at Deer Park, “to be Safe, Happy and Successful”.
Our Values
To achieve the Aims for our pupils and to reinforce a culture which helps us complete our daily Mission, pupils and staff have decided on the Deer Park values which will underpin all that we do. These are Trust, Kindness and Determination.
Trust ensures pupils feel safe, Kindness ensures pupils are happy and Determination leads to pupils being successful. And for our staff, working in a culture of Trust, Kindness and Determination helps us fulfil our Mission.
Our Ethos
How we talk, act and learn is built upon our values of Trust, Kindness and Determination. We are proud of each other, we are a positive community and our learning matters. This is the way in which we bring these values to life to ensure the culture at Deer Park in which we achieve more than we all first think is possible.
Read more about How We Talk…
Home School Agreement
Parents and pupils are invited to sign our partnership agreement, the Home School Agreement (see below), which sets out the expectations that should exist between home and school and this forms the basis of our ‘learning triangle’. These expectations are based on our School Standards and reflect our shared values.
We aim to work collaboratively with all pupils and parents to ensure the best outcomes for an individual. We recognise that at times emotions may run high. However, we do not expect any of our staff to be subjected to unacceptable behaviour and will take action to protect staff from this behaviour, including that which is abusive, offensive or threatening in line with the Home School Agreement that parents have signed. The Home School Agreement states that parents will support the actions of the school, respect and co-operate with the teachers and be polite, using appropriate language.

Welcome to Year 7
We are delighted that your child has been offered, and has accepted, a place at our school for September.
On behalf of all our staff and the wider school community, we are pleased to extend a very warm welcome to you and your family.
Transitioning to secondary school is an important milestone that can bring a mixture of excitement and nerves, and we want to reassure you that we are committed to supporting your child every step of the way.
We are confident that they will settle quickly into our friendly and nurturing environment.
On this page you will find useful information and links to other relevant areas of our website.

As Year Leader, my role is to provide pastoral care and support for all Year 7 students, ensuring they feel settled and confident as they transition into secondary school. Over the coming months, I will be visiting select primary schools, attending the welcome evenings, and working closely with students during the induction days to help make this transition as smooth and positive as possible.
I am committed to getting to know each student as an individual and working in partnership with parents and carers to support their wellbeing and success throughout the year”.

Applying for a Place
Please click on the type of place you are applying for:
A Year 7 Place
(Starting school at the beginning of September in Year 7)
We appreciate that the transition from primary to secondary school can be a cause of anxiety for both parents and pupils; however, we aim to help you make an informed decision about the next stage in your child’s education.
Open Events
We encourage everyone to visit Deer Park at one of our Open Events, which are open to all prospective students and their parents or carers.
We look forward to meeting you and introducing you to our school:
Open Mornings – 9:15 – 11 am
Open Evening – 5 – 7.30 pm
Wednesday 16th September 2026
Thursday 24th September 2026
Thursday 1st October 2026
Wednesday 30th September
Important Dates
For current Year 5 pupils
The deadline for secondary school applications for current Year 5 pupils is 31st October 2026.
For current Year 6 pupils
Secondary school places were confirmed on 2 March 2026. If your childwas successfully allocated a place at Deer Park, we are delighted toWelcome you and invite you to visit our ‘Welcome to Year 7’ page here.
Frequently Asked Questions
How do I apply for a place at Cirencester Deer Park School on transition from Primary School to Secondary School?
To be considered for a place at Deer Park, you must include the school amongst the five school preferences you are entitled to make through completion of your Common Application Form – further information can be found at www.gloucestershire.gov.uk/schooladmissions. Preferences should be ranked in priority order. If you are successful in gaining a place at your first preference school, none of your other choices will be considered.
How are places at Cirencester Deer Park School allocated?
Up to 209 places will be allocated at the School based on our Admissions Criteria which can be accessed on our Admissions Policy.
What if I live outside of your catchment area?
We know that there are insufficient pupils living within our catchment area to fill the secondary school places we have available. Places will be filled, up to the published admission number of 209, based on geographic proximity to the school, measured as a straight line distance from your home address to Reception at the School.
Will my son/daughter get a place?
If you submit your preference form by the deadline, live within our catchment area, and put Deer Park as your first choice, you will be allocated a place at the school.
If you live outside the catchment area, we cannot give any guarantees of a Year 7 place on Allocation Day. We were oversubscribed for Year 7 admissions in 2021-2024 and did hold appeals. However, by the start of September we were able to able to offer a place in Year 7 to everyone who wanted one, regardless of where they lived. Pupils often come to Deer Park from up to 15 miles away from the school.
What happens if I do not put Deer Park as my first preference?
The Local Authority will always allocate the highest ranked school that they can within your list of preferences. If Deer Park is your preferred school, it should always be listed as your first preference. If you list Deer Park lower in your preferences, and the Local Authority can allocate one of your higher preferences, you will not be offered a place at Deer Park. However, lower ranked schools are always considered as your ‘effective first preference’ if the Local Authority cannot allocate your higher preferences, so you are not prejudiced against in any way for placing a school lower down your preference form.
When will I hear if I have a place at Deer Park?
You will be advised by the Local Authority which School has been allocated for your son/daughter on National Allocation Day which is 2 March 2026.
What happens if my son/daughter does not get offered a place at Deer Park?
If you are unsuccessful in getting a place at Deer Park on National Allocation Day, you will have the opportunity to ask for ‘reconsideration’ through the Local Authority, which may result in a place being allocated by 6 April 2026. However, if this is unsuccessful, you will be placed on our waiting list, which is ranked based on geographic proximity to the School. You will also have the opportunity to go through the appeals process. Further information about this would follow. You are welcome to contact Danielle Clark, Head’s PA, on 01285 646558 to discuss this further.
What if I want to apply for a school place during the school year (in-year applications)?
Enquiries regarding ‘In Year Admissions’ should be made direct to Danielle Clark, Head’s PA at the School by email or by phone on 01285 646558. You can find further information on www.gloucestershire.gov.uk/schooladmissions.
When are your next Open Mornings?
In June/July we hold Open Mornings specifically for pupils in Year 5.
In September/October we hold two Open Mornings and one Open Evening which are open to all potential pupils and parents. Find out more…
In addition, Danielle Clark, Head’s PA, is happy to arrange mutually convenient tours of the school throughout the year and can be contacted by phone on 01285 646558 or by emailing enquiries@deerparkschool.net.
An In-Year Place
Starting a new school outside of the usual intake can also be daunting, but we have measures in place to help your child settle in quickly and comfortably.
Arrange a Tour
To arrange a personalised tour of the school, please contact Danielle Clark, Head’s PA by emailing enquiries@deerparkschool.net or by phone on 01285 646558.
How to Apply
(1) Complete an In-Year application form, which can be found here: In-year application form – AUG 2021 V3 or here In-year application form – AUG 2021, alternatively a paper copy can be collected from the school, or we can post one to you.
(2) Return your completed form to the school either via e-mail, by delivering it to Reception or by posting it to us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing & Digital Technology - Cirencester Deer Park School
pageCache.text:
Computing & Digital Technology
At Cirencester Deer Park School, our department’s mission is to “provide pupils with a challenging and engaging curriculum that equips them with the skills needed to navigate a rapidly changing world, leading to outstanding employment opportunities.” In response to the fast-evolving technological landscape, the Computing & Digital Technology department is undergoing a significant transformation. Our updated curriculum ensures it remains relevant, forward-thinking and aligned with the needs of both students and the wider workforce.
The curriculum now focuses on key areas such as Computer Science and a comprehensive range of end-user software. By integrating these subjects, we aim to provide pupils with a solid foundation in both the theoretical and practical aspects of technology. Pupils will develop a deeper understanding of computer systems, coding, algorithms and the application of these skills in real-world contexts.
Furthermore, the course includes essential software skills, ensuring that pupils are proficient in tools central to industries ranging from business to media and engineering. This practical approach prepares pupils to adapt to emerging technologies and equips them with the confidence to thrive in an increasingly digital world.
Whether pursuing higher education or entering the workforce directly, this curriculum will empower pupils to become innovative, adaptable and capable contributors in the tech-driven job market.
Over the course of three years, students will develop skills to become independent problem solvers, logical thinkers, and critical evaluators of technology’s impact on society. The curriculum fosters creativity in problem-solving, helping students approach challenges with a systematic and imaginative mindset.
As students gain practical knowledge in computing, they will also consider the ethical, social, and environmental implications of technology. By examining how technology influences various industries and society, students will become informed, responsible users of digital tools.
By the end of the course, students will be well-prepared for further study, with a strong foundation in critical thinking and real-world problem-solving.
For students seeking an intellectually stimulating challenge, we offer the AQA GCSE Computer Science course. This rigorous curriculum gives students a deep understanding of programming, algorithms, computer systems, networks and cybersecurity.
Throughout the course, pupils will explore fundamental concepts of modern computing, including hardware, software and how these components interact. They will gain hands-on experience designing and implementing algorithms (pseudocoding), as well as solving complex problems using Python, one of the most versatile programming languages.
The course is designed to prepare pupils for further study or careers in technology, developing their problem-solving techniques and computational thinking. It’s an ideal stepping stone for those who wish to pursue Computer Science at A Level or pursue on a career in the growing tech industry.
At Cirencester Deer Park School, we understand the importance of offering a diverse range of courses that not only engage pupils but also prepare them for future opportunities. The Eduqas Level 1/2 Vocational Award in Information Communication Technology is perfect for pupils who enjoy Computing & IT but prefer a less programming intensive approach.
This course allows pupils to explore topics like cybersecurity, the inner workings of the internet and how computer systems interact. These subjects are highly relevant in today’s digital world, and pupils will develop practical skills in using software tools such as Microsoft Excel for spreadsheet modelling, database management and digital application creation.
A key feature of this course is the Non-Examination Assessment (NEA), which accounts for 60% of the final grade. Through this assessment, pupils engage in real-world problem-solving and project management, developing vital skills in time management and client brief analysis.
This vocational qualification is an excellent option for pupils interested in business IT solutions, data management or digital project development, offering them hands-on, practical learning that leads to rewarding career pathways.
We offer a number of ways to enrich students’ experience of Computing and Digital Technology, helping them to connect classroom learning with real-world applications and even future opportunities in this fast-evolving subject.
As well as a Digital Futures workshop at Cirencester College and an EmPower Cyber workshop, we have taken groups to The University of Gloucestershire and the University of Oxford, where they learn about the huge range of further and higher education computing courses and employment opportunities available.
Every year our students enter the national Bebras Coding Challenge, run by the Raspberry Pi Foundation. This competition involves computational thinking, creativity, problem-solving skills and programmed solutions. Our students have historically performed exceptionally – at the top 10% of the country.
Computing Masterclasses
In recent years we have been fortunate to have been offered a place for four of our students across years 10 and 11 to attend the prestigious Royal Institution Masterclasses in Computer Science, supported by Morgan Stanley and the University of Oxford’s Department of Computer Science. Over the course of three months, our students dedicated their Saturday mornings to attending a series of engaging and thought-provoking workshops alongside like-minded young people from schools across the region. The masterclasses provided a unique and inspiring opportunity to explore a wide range of fascinating areas within Computer Science
This extra curricular club enables students to programme drones to fly a set course. By writing code, students translate abstract programming into immediate physical actions, developing practical skills in algorithms, sequencing, loops, and debugging. The club is due to start again in the academic year 2026-2027.

PSHEe
Through PSHEe (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education) pupils develop the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to manage their lives, now and in the future. We help pupils learn how to stay healthy, safe and prepared for life and work. In Key Stage 3 and 4, pupils have one PSHEe lesson a fortnight.
The curriculum is well resourced with materials coming from the Gloucestershire Healthy Living and Learning team, the PSHEe Association, Public Health England, and the Oak Academy. We have external contributions to our curriculum around issues such as Domestic Abuse.
Pupils in Key Stage 3 receive at least two lessons from our Schoolbeat officer, PC Davis. Currently, Year 7 are on Grooming and Drugs, including alcohol, Year 8 on Sexting and Exploitation and then, Year 9 on County Lines and Domestic Violence.
Please note that the curriculum is being updated in line with the Department for Education’s revised statutory guidance on Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE), due to be implemented from September 2026.

Expressive Arts
The Expressive Arts Faculty inspires a love of Music, Drama and Performing Arts in all pupils. We deliver a curriculum that helps pupils appreciate a range of different art forms, but simultaneously is a way to develop social and emotional intelligences. We provide opportunities for pupils to broaden their creativity and are an outward facing faculty enabling pupils to contribute to their local community.
Our curriculum is built on a spiral curriculum, revisiting skills each year to improve them, adding more detail and applying them to different situations.

Drama
We aim to use Drama as a tool to help develop our pupils into confident, creative individuals. The subject covers:
Find out about each Key Stage in Drama:
Key Stage 3 Drama
Drama incorporates Creating, Performing and Appraising skills. Pupils will learn through a range of topical based schemes of learning, in which pupils will have the opportunity to explore and develop these three important skills, as well as several key transferrable skills, such as building confidence, teamwork and listening and learning from others.
We aim for all pupils to embrace drama and enjoy learning in this practical approach.Drama lessons cover a range of diverse and challenging topics and texts at all stages.
See KS3 Drama Learning Journey below.
Key Stage 4 Drama
At Key Stage 4, we build on the skills and knowledge taught in Key Stage 3. The GCSE specification we follow is the AQA specification which we believe builds on the skills and philosophy acquired through Key Stage 3, whilst developing the pupils’ interest in Theatre.
During the course pupils will explore texts, understand the making of characters and how they interact in their relationships with other characters and the audience. As part of the course they will work with professional theatre practitioners. This will give the opportunity to refine performance skills. Pupils will be expected to perform to audiences such as a primary school or parents, go on at least one live theatre trip and attend rehearsals which will take place out of lessons.
Assessment is in three forms: Practical Class Work, Performance and Final Written Exam.
Component 1 – Final written Exam 40%
Section A: multiple choice. Section B: four questions on a given extract from the set play Blood Brothers. Section C: one two part question (from a choice) on the work of theatre makers in a single live theatre production.
Component 2 – Devising log and performance 40% Process of creating devised drama, performing the work, and analysing and evaluating it.
Component 3 – Practical coursework 20% Practical performances of two extracts from a play.

Celebrating 60 Years of Comprehensive Education in Cirencester
Generations of alumni came together to share memories
On Saturday 24th October, we opened the school to celebrate the diamond anniversary both of our school and of comprehensive education in Cirencester. It was a very special day, with several generations of alumni and staff coming together to browse the photos and memorabilia and share experiences over tea and cake.
Co-Headteacher Helen Howe said:
“We were delighted to see so many people return to Deer Park as part of our 60th anniversary celebrations to celebrate this important milestone and be part of Deer Park’s continuing story. It was a special occasion filled with reminiscence, laughter and shared memories. There was a real sense of pride and nostalgia as old friendships were rekindled, stories were exchanged and visitors saw how the school has evolved over the decades.”
Former Headteacher and former Head of the Corinium Education Trust, Chiquita Henson agreed:
“It was lovely to see so many from the local community reconnecting through a collaborative endeavour with Cirencester’s History Festival. I am really pleased that the commitment to and, importantly, celebration of, comprehensive education in Cirencester continues.”
The school we know now was formed by the amalgamation of the Grammar School on Victoria Road and the two ‘modern’ schools at the ‘Deer Park’ in 1966, but many events in the history of our town and the evolution of education, led to this point:

pageCache.pageTitle: Deer Park Writers Scoop Top Prizes in Story Writing Competition - Cirencester Deer Park School
pageCache.text:
Deer Park Writers Scoop Top Prizes in Story Writing Competition
Bringing to life women and girls' voices from the past.
Last month the Cirencester and District branch of Soroptimist International invited KS4 and KS5 story writers from the area to pen a short story with the theme ‘Her Story: Women and Girls’ Voices from the Past’. The brief was to write a story of between 500 and 1000 words which transported the reader into the world of a woman or girl from the past through a vivid, authentic voice. The Soroptimists say ‘From Queens to codebreakers, scientists to spies, poets to protestors, women and girls have always shaped our world’.
We are delighted to share that although some of their fellow competitors were older college students, Deer Park entrants scooped first and third place, plus two ‘highly commended’.
Librarian, Mrs Trusty, encouraged and collated entries and even held a small celebration with cakes and personalised feedback ahead of the prize-giving ceremony at Cirencester Library on 23rd October.
At the ceremony, these young people found that their writing had not only won a prize, but that their stories had been published in an anthology, which they each received a copy of.
Congratulations to Sasha, Natasha, Ella and Mimi – don’t stop telling stories that should be heard.
Click to read the Cirencester Soroptimist’s write-up about the competition
Third prize: Natasha C for ‘Grace O’Malley’

Partnerships
Deer Park Primary Sports Partnership
Deer Park School’s Primary Sports Partnership was established in 2004 with the aim of supporting local primary schools to provide a high quality programme of physical education, in line with Government targets. In addition, the partnership aims to maximise participation in competitive sport by providing a varied range of extra-curricular competitions and festivals for students in Key Stage 1 and 2, whilst signposting local sporting opportunities.
The Partnership’s vision for all schools within Cirencester is that physical education is seen as an important aspect of school life, making a significant contribution to the personal well-being, academic development and overall enjoyment of school life. For this reason, the ‘Deer Park Primary Sports Partnership’ endeavour to support partner schools in the provision of an outstanding, innovative physical education curriculum that inspires the development of a culture where pupils, together with the wider community, engage in physical activity and develop a lifelong active lifestyle.
The current programme includes a variety of sporting activities such as Football, Netball, Multi-sports, Cross-country and Athletics. Deer Park also hosts the Area Primary Athletics which involves the best primary pupils in the county competing. This allows primary pupils to develop key sporting and physical skills such as speed, agility and endurance in a fun and competitive manner.
All primary sports competitions and festivals at Deer Park involve the use of our Sports Leaders to help organise and manage each event. The Year 9 Young Leaders, through specific training, help with organising and managing each event. Roles and responsibilities include coaching, officiating and the administration. This allows pupils to develop key skills including communication and teamwork.
GITEP
Cirencester Deer Park has a long history of delivering high quality Initial Teacher Training in partnership with the Gloucestershire Initial Teacher Education Partnership (GITEP). GITEP is a unique collaboration between all the secondary schools in Gloucestershire and the University of Gloucestershire. The GITEP programme is designed to recruit, train and retain the best teachers for our partnership schools. Almost 100 trainees completed the programme across Gloucestershire last year and all are employed in schools, well over half within our partnership. Employment and completion rates are both well above the national average.
For more information on Training to be a teacher, go to the GITEP website.

Library & Reading
Our large and vibrant Library, also known as Powell’s Learning Centre or the PLC, forms a valued central resource within the school, providing study and research facilities and many additional services for all pupils and staff. With over 10,000 carefully selected resources on a wide variety of subjects, we are sure there is something for everyone. We use Access-it Library Computer lending system which makes selecting and finding books very easy.
Pupils can use the library for quiet reading, studying and doing homework, researching, computer work or looking at magazines and newspapers.
We have a small number of Key Stage 3 Pupil Librarians who help the librarians at break and lunchtime. Pupils can apply to be a pupil librarian in September/ October.

Readathons
Since 2015 our Librarians have combined World Book Day with a Readathon, when pupils, generally in Years 7-10, are given the opportunity to spend half a day or whole day in our library, The PLC, reading. No lessons, just reading for the pleasure of reading! Reading and raising money through their Readathon for Read for Good, a local charity who provide books and stories for children in hospital across the country. It’s a great opportunity for anyone who loves to read. Did you know that Deer Park is an ‘Outstanding Readathon School‘. Incredibly, due to generous donations, we have raised over £20,000 from our Readathons since 1995! Read about our 2026 Readathon here.
“Reading for pleasure is the single biggest indicator of a child’s future success – more than their family circumstances, their parents’ educational background or their income.”
Reading is breathing for the mind
Making time and space for reading can make SUCH a difference to us all, both mentally and physically.
Reading is a great way to relax. Did you know that reading has been shown to work better and faster to calm frazzled nerves than listening to music, going for a walk or sitting down with a cup of tea? Because the human mind has to concentrate on reading, the distraction eases the tensions in muscles and the heart. And so we feel more relaxed. Perhaps going for a walk and then, when back, sitting down to read, with a cup of tea, is the way to go!
When you read, not only do you reduce your stress levels, you also have the ability to escape from what immediately surrounds you. In addition, you learn more and become more able to understand others’ beliefs, feelings and thoughts i.e. you become more empathetic.
We encourage EVERYONE, no matter your age, to read for at least 20 minutes each day.
Recommended Reading Lists:
Our English Faculty has helpfully categorised their reading lists e.g. historical, dystopian, thriller, realistic, coming of age, and more. Download the lists by clicking on the images below and look for inspiration. How many of these books have you read or will you read this year?
Pupil and staff recent recommendations:
Facing the Frozen Ocean by Bear Grylls
Recommended read from a pupil who liked how it was full of suspense and adventure.
This is the true story about Bear Grylls, a famous British survival adventurer, and his dream of crossing the treacherous north Atlantic in an open inflatable boat. As you start to read this book you feel like you are one of the men on the mission. Bear Grylls tells his true story with such passion that you feel you are with him in that small little boat as waves keep on hitting your face.
A Monster Calls by Patrick Ness
Geography teacher, Miss Bluett says of this book: I picked this up for a quick look after a recommendation from a friend and 2 hours later was still reading! It is a powerful story of coping and letting go and just like Conor in the book I wasn’t ready for the Monster’s tales to end.
Born to Run by Michael Morpurgo
Many of our younger pupils enjoy books by Michael Morpurgo and ‘Born to Run’ seems to be a particular favourite. This story is about a greyhound who finds himself in difficult situations. However, he is continually rescued and makes new friends on his adventures.
Girl, Woman, Other by Bernadine Evaristo
Review by English teacher Mrs Voss.
I thought it was a uniquely told, inspiring tale of the lives of twelve women. Evaristo has weaved their stories together in an honest and original narrative which spans across generations. Winner of the Booker Prize 2019 and a fantastic read!
The Tattooist of Auschwitz by Heather Morris
Summary by English teacher Mrs Voss.
A heart-breaking story of a man who lived through one of the harrowing periods in living history. Ultimately a tale of survival and love amongst horror and suffering. Definitely worth a read.
The Girl You Left Behind by Jojo Moyes
Mrs Voss, English teacher, says: A beautifully written tale of two different women living in two different generations. They share the love of one painting and the history behind it reveals a shocking truth. Moyes cleverly links the lives of these very different characters and uncovers some dark revelations about survival in a war-torn existence.
Where the Crawdads Sing by Delia Owens
Review by English teacher Mrs Voss.
This was an excellent read. You are thrown into the world of a truly inspiring heroine who you cannot help but adore. Owens captures the unexpected beauty in the natural setting so beautifully. The mystery element to the novel makes it very difficult to put down – I thoroughly recommend this!
The Salt Path by Raynor Winn
Recommendation from Librarian Mrs Burton.
A true story about a middle aged couple who are made homeless through no fault of their own. Raynor’s husband Moth is diagnosed with a terrible untreatable illness. What do they decide to do? Pick up a tent , pack their rucksacks and walk the South West Coastal Path, wild camping and living on £48 a week.

Reading for Good
Students spend the day reading for pleasure, changing lives in the process
55 students from Years 7 to 10 spent a whole day reading for pleasure this week, as part of the Read for Good Readathon.
Having gained sponsorship pledges and chosen their books, students settled down in the school library on a comfy chair or beanbag and escaped into a different world. For one day only they were permitted to rearrange furniture and use blankets to construct reading dens to snuggle up in. Stopping only for breaks and hot chocolate and biscuits, this was a chance to take a break from timetables and indulge in the simple joy of reading.
The money raised by this event buys books and funds storyteller visits for our nearest children’s hospital, it also helps to stock our own library as the school receives a voucher for use at the Scholastic Book Club.
Research conducted in a partnership between BookTrust and the Open University found that children who read are more likely to succeed academically and emotionally.
We ask that all Year 8 students carry a reading book in their bag at all times, ensuring they always have something purposeful to engage with during reading opportunities, tutor time, or any moment of downtime. Having a book readily available also helps us build a consistent reading culture and gives students frequent chances to practise and enjoy reading. There is nothing to stop other year groups doing the same.
There are fiction, non-fiction and graphic novels to suit every taste and we publish a recommended reading list for each key stage, which can be accessed by clicking below.

The Science Faculty is based in the purpose-built Powell’s Centre. There are eight well-equipped labs, two with ICT facilities and dataloggers. The Science Faculty teaching staff are enthusiastic, dedicated and hugely experienced. Some of the Science Staff also have previous industrial or academic experience. We all believe in the value of practical and investigative work, and the Science teaching staff are well supported by a team of Science Technicians. We have worked hard with our pupils to return Outstanding Science GCSE results for more than a decade.

Key Stage 3 Science
Our pupils follow the National Curriculum for Science.
Our Schemes of Learning have been enhanced by our own practicals and demonstrations, to make our pupils’ lessons more varied, relevant and accessible. Pupils’ skills in Numeracy are explicitly developed in many of our lessons to help to build this fundamental key skill. We try hard to maintain a sense of ‘awe and wonder’ in Science and the World around us and promote independent thinking that allows pupils to consider themselves as part of something larger – within the UK and the wider world. Pupils in Science study a ‘spiral curriculum’ in which key concepts are revisited and built upon.
In the document below, the topics covered in Years 7 to 9 are outlined, together with particularly strong examples of opportunities in Numeracy (‘N’), ‘Awe and Wonder (‘A’) and relevance to life in modern Britain (‘GB’).

Key Stage 4 Science
Our Key Stage 4 offer allows every pupil to pursue a course that is suitable for their ability and interests. Separate Sciences (Biology, Chemistry and Physics) and Combined Science follow a ‘traditional’ pattern. Scientific content is taught in a series of short modules and assessed in terminal exams at the end of Year 11. Assessment is based on 100% examination.
Pupils have a choice of either:
‘AQA GCSE Combined Science: Trilogy’ (two GCSEs) in 10 lessons a fortnight (20% of curriculum time); Find out more…
‘AQA GCSE Separate Sciences’ in which Biology Chemistry and Physics are taught as individual subjects (three GCSEs) in 15 lessons a fortnight (30% of curriculum time)
Find out more about the Learning Journey of each Science below:
There are many opportunities for pupils to engage in extra-curricular activities in Science.
At Key Stage 3 we offer a STEM Club, with opportunities for pupils to complete Crest awards. We have also held a ‘Space Day’ with examples of genuine Moon rocks and many other exhibits relating to Space and Space Exploration. At GCSE level we have offered visits for pupils to Oxford Natural History Museum, Bristol University Chemistry Department and Bath University (DNA workshop). We extend invitations to other specialists to give presentations or run workshops for our other Key Stage 4 pupils. Most recently, our Separate Science classes were visited by researchers in Nuclear Physics and met a robotic dog that could be used to monitor radiation sources safely.
